title: The ePlane Company selects LYNX MOSA.ic to run mixed criticality software side by side on e200X eVTOL
summary: The e200X is a three-seat lift and cruise eVTOL with a modular airframe designed for air ambulance, urban cargo, and passenger service.
body_markdown:
Lynx, a leader in safe and secure software platforms for mission-critical edge systems, today announced at eVTOL Show USA that The ePlane Company has selected LYNX MOSA.ic as the mixed-criticality software platform for mission computing on its e200X eVTOL.


The e200X is a three-seat (pilot plus two passengers) lift and cruise eVTOL with a modular airframe designed for air ambulance, urban cargo, and passenger service. Each variant carries a different payload, sensor set, and software stack, while flight control stays deterministic and certifiable in every configuration.


LYNX MOSA.ic partitions the e200X’s onboard compute so flight-critical software, such as the vehicle and energy management systems, runs in ARINC 653 partitions, isolated from lower-criticality mission functions that handle sensor data processing and situational awareness inference.


Heavy AI processing runs on a separate platform, and the mission system supplies the controlled interfaces between that platform and the rest of the aircraft, ensuring clear cybersecurity and safety isolation.


“A multi-role aircraft asks more of its computers than a single-mission design, because the mission software keeps changing while flight control cannot,” said Tim Reed, chief executive officer of Lynx.“LYNX MOSA.ic lets ePlane keep flight-critical software isolated and certifiable while its pilot assist software evolves with each role.”


LYNX MOSA.ic is a mixed-criticality operating environment built around a separation kernel-based type 1 hypervisor. It gives each software subject its own space and time partition, so applications at different levels of criticality can share one platform, and it is certifiable to DO-178C DAL A.


“Urban air mobility is as much a computational challenge as it is an aerodynamic one. Operating high-density routes safely across emergency response, logistics, and passenger transit requires mission computing that is both certifiably safe and functionally modular. LYNX MOSA.ic gives us the deterministic partitioning required to isolate safety-critical systems while our engineers build cutting-edge aircraft functionalities on familiar tools. It is a foundational technology for delivering scalable, multi-role electric aviation,” said Prof. Satya Chakravarthy, founder and technical lead, The ePlane Company.


Lynx was scheduled to take the stage at eVTOL Show USA on Tuesday, November 17, at 11:35 a.m. in the Gateway Ballroom at the Santa Clara Convention Center to present “Building the Certifiable Software Behind Electric Flight.” Attendees are also invited to connect with the Lynx team at Booth #33.


*This press release was prepared and distributed by The ePlane Co.*
